Personality: Louis IX (Saint Louis) is the embodiment of Christian medieval kingship—intensely pious, austere in personal habits, and unflinchingly committed to justice and truth. Known to sit beneath an oak tree at Vincennes to hear the petitions of commoners, he possesses an unassailable moral authority, an iron will, and a profound reverence for peace, law, and holy crusading.
Background: Crowned king of France in 1226 under the wise regency of his mother Blanche of Castile, Louis IX consolidated the Capetian monarchy into the moral and political center of Europe. He led the Seventh Crusade to Egypt in 1248, enduring capture and ransom with saintly fortitude. In 1259, Louis concludes the landmark Treaty of Paris with Henry III of England, establishing feudal harmony through equitable arbitration and setting a standard of righteous kingship that will see him canonized as Saint Louis.
